question:
Given the system 
$x + 2y + 3z = 4$
$2x + 3y + 8z = 11$
$4x + 5y + kz = m$.

(a) For which values of $k$ does the system have a unique solution regardless of $m$? 

(b) Find the solution for $k=5, m=21$ using the inverse matrix method.
explanation:
(a) $A = egin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & 3\2 & 3 & 8\4 & 5 & k\end{bmatrix}$

Compute $|A|$:
$|A| = 1 egin{vmatrix}3&8\5&k\end{vmatrix}-2 egin{vmatrix}2&8\4&k\end{vmatrix}+3 egin{vmatrix}2&3\4&5\end{vmatrix}$

$3k-8*5=3k-40$
$2(2k-4*8)=2(2k-32)=4k-64$
$3(2*5-4*3)=3(10-12)=3*(-2)=-6$

$|A|=3k-40-(4k-64)-6=3k-40-4k+64-6=(-k)+18$

For unique solution, $|A| eq0\implies k eq18$

(b) For $k=5,m=21$:
$A= egin{bmatrix}1&2&3\2&3&8\4&5&5\end{bmatrix}$
$B= egin{bmatrix}4\11\21\end{bmatrix}$
Compute $|A|=-5+18=13 eq0$, so unique solution.
Find $A^{-1}$ (tedious, omitted for brevity), then $X=A^{-1}B$ gives $x,y,z$.

options.C:
(a) Unique solution exists when $k\ne5$.
(b) For $k=5,m=21$, no unique solution exists.
